small_guidance:
- The kernel currently launches only N*C = 16*128 = 2048 programs each reducing S = 20*36*36 = 25920 elements; this under-utilizes the 4090. Split the reduction across multiple programs per (n,c) using a 2D grid `(N*C, num_s_tiles)` with `atomic_add` into the output, or use a tree reduction with a small BLOCK_S (e.g. 256/512/1024) and many programs.
- Drop the oversized BLOCK_S configs (8192–32768) — S is only ~26K so most lanes are masked-off. Add configs with BLOCK_S in {256, 512, 1024, 2048} and num_warps in {2, 4, 8}; the inner loop should iterate a few times to hide latency.
- Fuse the `invstd/scale/bias` precompute into a tiny prologue kernel (or compute inline per-program) to avoid the small but non-trivial host-side torch ops on every forward.
large_guidance:
- The torch `ConvTranspose3d` now dominates runtime (the post-conv fused kernel is fine). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)` that loads an input tile and scatter-adds `input × weight` outer products into the (D+kd-1, H+kh-1, W+kw-1) output grid, folding `scale_factor` and BN affine (`scale`, `bias`) into the conv bias epilogue, then doing the global-average reduction in a second tiny kernel — or even accumulating per-(n,c) sums directly during the scatter so GAP is free.
- Alternative design: gather-style conv-transpose where one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)` loops over `(ic, kd, kh, kw)` and pulls from input with the transposed index math (`(o + pad - k) % stride == 0`). Use `channels_last_3d` layout so IC/OC are the contiguous GEMM-K/N axes; tile as a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC) GEMM with autotune over {32,64,128} × {4,8} warps.
- Since the final output is `(N, C, 1, 1, 1)`, consider a single persistent kernel that computes the conv-transpose output element-by-element but only accumulates the per-(n, oc) sum (never materializing the (N,C,20,36,36) tensor). This converts the whole forward into a reduction of shape `(N, OC) ← sum over (IC, kd, kh, kw, d_in, h_in, w_in)` with the BN affine applied at the end — massive memory-traffic win.
